standard_prerequisites.name: The forcing question, the space of relations and its correspondence with bounded functions
standard_prerequisites.statement: The section fixes a condition, a formula, and a relation space whose members are relations between finite sets of natural numbers and natural numbers, bounded by a computable function, and in one-to-one correspondence with the constrained functions: to a function one attaches the relation of the pairs lying in its values, and conversely. The forcing question holds for a condition and a formula when for every relation of that space there is a finite block inside the reservoir that is free for the corresponding function and makes the formula hold on the enlarged stem; the formula considered here is of the lowest syntactic complexity, so its truth is witnessed by a finite amount of information. The author's own definition and the two lemmas of the section about the forcing question and its specification are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the step that turns the second-order formulation of the forcing question into a first-order statement about one level of bounded progressive functions, which is what makes the generic filter construction effective.

core_obligations: First direction: assume the first-order statement, that is, fix a level such that every bounded progressive function on that level admits a finite free block in the reservoir making the formula hold; take an arbitrary relation of the bounded space, truncate its corresponding function to that level, and note that the truncation is again bounded and progressive, so it admits such a block; the same block is free for the untruncated function, and since the relation was arbitrary the forcing question holds (source lines 1206-1207).

Second direction: assume the first-order statement fails, so at every level there is a bounded progressive function on that level such that no free block in the reservoir makes the formula hold, and collect those functions level by level into a tree ordered by extension (source line 1209, first sentence).

Apply Konig's lemma: the tree is finitely branching, so it has an infinite path; that path is a bounded function such that no finite free block in the reservoir makes the formula hold, and the relation attached to it witnesses that the forcing question fails (source line 1209, second and third sentences).

proof_roadmap.step: First direction: truncate an arbitrary relation's function to the level supplied by the first-order statement and reuse the witnessing block.
Second direction: build the tree of counterexamples level by level.
Konig's lemma gives an infinite path, whose attached relation witnesses the failure of the forcing question.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:fs-forcing-question-sigma01（源 1201-1204 行，证明 1205-1210 行）：对 condition (f,σ,X) 与 Σ^0_1 公式 φ(G)，(f,σ,X) ⊩ φ(G) 当且仅当存在 k∈ω 使每个 b_f^+-constrained progressive 函数 g:[0,k]^{≤h(·)}→[0,k]^{<ω} 都有有限的 g-free ρ ⊆ X↾_k 使其 φ(σ∪ρ) 成立。关键操作不是例行核验：正向要把任意关系 R∈R_{b_f^+} 对应的函数 g_R **截断到 [0,k]**，并论证截断后仍 constrained 且 progressive，从而「截断版的见证 ρ 对原 g_R 也 free」——这一步用到 free 性只依赖 [0,k] 以下的取值（1206-1207 行）；反向要构造「第 k 层装所有反例 g_k」的树，用有限分叉 + **König 引理**取无穷路径 g，再取对应关系 R_g 作为反证见证（1209 行）。难点在于把二阶量化的 forcing question 化归为单个层次的初等陈述，且两个方向分别用「截断」与「树 + König」两种完全不同的工具；原文位置在证明的 1206-1207、1209 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:fs-forcing-question-sigma01 at source lines 1201-1204 together with its proof at source lines 1205-1210, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This source ships no separate preamble file, so the retained preamble is sliced mechanically from the pinned file by the lane and is shared, byte for byte, with the other cards of this source; it carries the authors' full macro block, including the symbols for the forcing relation, for the tree and for the space of functions that the retained statement and proof use.

The retained preamble is the lane's shared slice for this source; it was extended during this card's first revision to carry the three macros for calligraphic R, S and T, which in the source sit just after the theorem declarations and which the statement of this lemma needs. The first revision failed on exactly that undefined macro, and this revision is the corrected one.

One context span carries the definition of the forcing question at source lines 1194-1197, which the retained statement names; it is context, not a counted unit, and it does not overlap the counted interval.

The retained statement and proof contain no reference to another labelled result of the article and no citation: the only external ingredient is the standard form of Konig's lemma applied to the finitely branching tree of counterexamples, which the author names in passing and which is recorded in the standard prerequisites. Accordingly this card carries no navigation pointer and no bibliography entry.

The article states immediately above the counted lemma that the forcing question as defined is of second-order complexity, and the counted lemma is its first-order reformulation; that surrounding prose is not part of the counted unit and is not retained.
